```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# message=FALSE/warning=FALSE (those settings only kept them out of the HTML,
# which nobody reads). GitHub timestamps each log line, so the log shows how
# long each step took (2026-11-13: a WY run stalled with nothing to go on).
```

# Scrapes Montana's K-12 and higher-ed job postings, salary, and staffing data and combines them into the datasets
# Mt_Ed_Jobs/app.R reads. Mirrors the Wyoming Education Jobs Dashboard's Wy_ED_Jobs.Rmd.

## Part 1: Montana K-12 Data

### K-12 districts scraped directly (AppliTrack, SchoolSpring, Tyler Portico, TedK12)
```{r k12 direct-platform districts, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(chromote)
library(edjobs)
source("direct_api_scrapers.R")
source("misc_district_scrapers.R")

registry <- read_k12_registry()

# AppliTrack -- output columns (title/position/position2/date_posted/
# location/closing_date) already match combinedclean's shape closely; only
# District needs adding.
applitrack_districts <- registry[registry$Platform == "AppliTrack", ]
applitrack_results <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(applitrack_districts)), function(i) {
  row <- applitrack_districts[i, ]
  df <- safe_scrape(
    row$District,
    scrape_fn = function() fetch_applitrack_postings(row$Platform_Key),
    expected_cols = c("title", "position", "position2", "date_posted", "location", "closing_date")
  )
  if (nrow(df) > 0) df$District <- row$District
  df
})
# url is the posting's own AppliTrack page, built from its job ID
# (applitrack_posting_url()), so each posting is identified by it rather than
# by its title; the district's board URL only when no job ID was read.
# Close_Date is the board's "Closing Date" as written ("open until filled"
# or a date; raw archive and combinedclean).
applitrack_raw <- bind_rows(applitrack_results)
if (nrow(applitrack_raw) > 0) {
  applitrack_df <- applitrack_raw %>%
    # A failed scrape's safe_scrape() placeholder has no Pay_* columns.
    ensure_posted_pay_columns() %>%
    mutate(job_id = if ("job_id" %in% names(.)) job_id else NA_character_,
           closing_date = if ("closing_date" %in% names(.)) closing_date else NA_character_) %>%
    left_join(select(applitrack_districts, District, Platform_Key, Job_Link), by = "District") %>%
    transmute(title, date_posted, position = NA_character_, location,
              url = coalesce(applitrack_posting_url(Platform_Key, job_id), Job_Link), District,
              Posting_Source = "AppliTrack (direct district board)",
              Close_Date = closing_date,
              Pay_Min, Pay_Max, Pay_Unit, Pay_Text)
} else {
  applitrack_df <- data.frame(title = character(0), date_posted = character(0), position = character(0),
                              location = character(0), url = character(0), District = character(0),
                              Posting_Source = character(0), Close_Date = character(0))
}

# SchoolSpring / Tyler Portico -- same output shape (Title/Location/
# Posted_Date/Link), position is always recomputed from title downstream so
# it's set NA_character_ here rather than kept from the source (matching
# Wyoming's springer/SchoolSpring chunk's own convention).
schoolspring_districts <- registry[registry$Platform == "SchoolSpring", ]
schoolspring_results <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(schoolspring_districts)), function(i) {
  row <- schoolspring_districts[i, ]
  df <- safe_scrape(
    row$District,
    scrape_fn = function() fetch_schoolspring_postings(row$Platform_Key),
    expected_cols = c("Title", "Location", "Posted_Date", "Link")
  )
  if (nrow(df) > 0) df$District <- row$District
  df
})
schoolspring_df <- bind_rows(schoolspring_results)
# Each posting's own record adds Close_Date (the deadline applicants see; NA
# for "Posted until filled"), Job_Status (raw archive only) and posted pay
# (add_schoolspring_details()). A failed detail request leaves only that
# posting's fields NA.
if (nrow(schoolspring_df) > 0 && "Link" %in% names(schoolspring_df)) {
  schoolspring_df <- add_schoolspring_details(schoolspring_df)
}
if (nrow(schoolspring_df) > 0) {
  schoolspring_df <- schoolspring_df %>%
    ensure_posted_pay_columns() %>%
    transmute(title = Title, date_posted = Posted_Date, position = NA_character_,
              location = Location, url = Link, District,
              Posting_Source = "SchoolSpring (direct district board)",
              Close_Date = if ("Close_Date" %in% names(.)) Close_Date else NA_character_,
              Job_Status = if ("Job_Status" %in% names(.)) Job_Status else NA_character_,
              Pay_Min, Pay_Max, Pay_Unit, Pay_Text)
} else {
  schoolspring_df <- data.frame(title = character(0), date_posted = character(0), position = character(0),
                                 location = character(0), url = character(0), District = character(0),
                                 Posting_Source = character(0), Close_Date = character(0))
}

tylerportico_districts <- registry[registry$Platform == "TylerPortico", ]
tylerportico_results <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(tylerportico_districts)), function(i) {
  row <- tylerportico_districts[i, ]
  df <- safe_scrape(
    row$District,
    scrape_fn = function() fetch_tylerportico_postings(row$Platform_Key, row$District),
    expected_cols = c("Title", "Location", "Posted_Date", "Link")
  )
  if (nrow(df) > 0) df$District <- row$District
  df
})
tylerportico_df <- bind_rows(tylerportico_results)
if (nrow(tylerportico_df) > 0) {
  tylerportico_df <- tylerportico_df %>%
    transmute(title = Title, date_posted = Posted_Date, position = NA_character_,
              location = Location, url = Link, District,
              Posting_Source = "Tyler Portico (direct district board)",
              Close_Date = if ("Close_Date" %in% names(.)) Close_Date else NA_character_,   # real end dates only
              Job_Code = if ("Job_Code" %in% names(.)) Job_Code else NA_character_)   # OPI matching key (raw archive only)
} else {
  tylerportico_df <- data.frame(title = character(0), date_posted = character(0), position = character(0),
                                 location = character(0), url = character(0), District = character(0),
                                 Posting_Source = character(0), Job_Code = character(0))
}

# TedK12 -- output columns (title/date_posted/position/location/url) already
# match combinedclean's shape; only District needs adding.
tedk12_districts <- registry[registry$Platform == "TedK12", ]
tedk12_results <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(tedk12_districts)), function(i) {
  row <- tedk12_districts[i, ]
  df <- safe_scrape(
    row$District,
    scrape_fn = function() fetch_tedk12_postings(row$Platform_Key),
    expected_cols = c("title", "date_posted", "position", "location", "url")
  )
  if (nrow(df) > 0) df$District <- row$District
  df
})
tedk12_df <- bind_rows(tedk12_results)
if (nrow(tedk12_df) == 0) {
  tedk12_df <- data.frame(title = character(0), date_posted = character(0), position = character(0),
                           location = character(0), url = character(0), District = character(0),
                           Posting_Source = character(0))
} else {
  tedk12_df <- tedk12_df %>%
    mutate(Posting_Source = "TedK12 (direct district board)")
}

# Red Rover (St. Ignatius, Hamilton, Columbia Falls) -- the GraphQL API Red
# Rover's own board calls (edjobs::fetch_redrover_postings(), 0.14.0; WY's
# fetcher). Platform_Key is the board's numeric org ID; the link slug comes from
# Job_Link. Read with Chrome inside the Apptegy batch until 2026-11, which gave
# a per-posting link to only some postings; every row now carries its own
# /opening/<n> page and the board's posted pay. A posting with no location
# takes the district's city, as the Chrome parser did.
redrover_districts <- registry[registry$Platform == "RedRoverK12", ]
redrover_results <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(redrover_districts)), function(i) {
  row <- redrover_districts[i, ]
  df <- safe_scrape(
    row$District,
    scrape_fn = function() fetch_redrover_postings(row$Platform_Key, redrover_org_slug(row$Job_Link)),
    expected_cols = c("Title", "Location", "Posted_Date", "Posting_ID", "Link")
  )
  if (nrow(df) > 0) {
    df$District <- row$District
    df$Location <- dplyr::coalesce(dplyr::na_if(trimws(df$Location), ""), row$City)
  }
  df
})
redrover_df <- bind_rows(redrover_results)
if (nrow(redrover_df) > 0) {
  redrover_df <- redrover_df %>%
    ensure_posted_pay_columns() %>%
    transmute(title = Title, date_posted = Posted_Date, position = NA_character_,
              location = Location, url = Link, District,
              Posting_Source = "Red Rover (direct district board)",
              Pay_Min, Pay_Max, Pay_Unit, Pay_Text)
} else {
  redrover_df <- data.frame(title = character(0), date_posted = character(0), position = character(0),
                            location = character(0), url = character(0), District = character(0),
                            Posting_Source = character(0))
}

# St. Labre Indian School's Trakstar board (fetch_st_labre_postings(), direct_api_scrapers.R; 2026-11-23): three
# private Catholic schools (St. Labre, Ashland; St. Charles Mission, Pryor; Pretty Eagle Catholic Academy, Saint
# Xavier), not in the registry (they have no NCES LEAID) and on the map from other_employers.csv. Each posting's own
# page gives its posted date and the pay grade.
st_labre_df <- safe_scrape(
  "St Labre Indian H S",
  scrape_fn = function() fetch_st_labre_postings(),
  expected_cols = c("Title", "Location", "Posted_Date", "Link", "District")
)
if (nrow(st_labre_df) > 0) {
  st_labre_df <- st_labre_df %>%
    ensure_posted_pay_columns() %>%
    transmute(title = Title, date_posted = Posted_Date, position = NA_character_,
              location = Location, url = Link, District,
              Posting_Source = "Trakstar (St. Labre's school board)",
              Close_Date = if ("Close_Date" %in% names(.)) Close_Date else NA_character_,
              Pay_Min, Pay_Max, Pay_Unit, Pay_Text)
} else {
  st_labre_df <- data.frame(title = character(0), date_posted = character(0), position = character(0),
                            location = character(0), url = character(0), District = character(0),
                            Posting_Source = character(0))
}

# Every other directly read board (46 platforms: the one-off district scrapers and the CMS families) goes through
# edjobs::scrape_registry_platforms() (edjobs 0.92.0, review step 5 slice 4, 2026-11-24): each registry row is
# scraped with its scraper_spec() from state_config.R (the same call the live check and scripts/repro_scraper.R
# make) and labelled with the registry's Posting_Source column (blank: "<District> site (direct board)"). One
# group per platform, in MT_DIRECT_BOARD_PLATFORMS's order; each group's dates are parsed together, as the
# per-platform blocks this replaced did. A district on one of these platforms is a registry row, with no code here.
direct_board_dfs <- scrape_registry_platforms(registry, MT_DIRECT_BOARD_PLATFORMS,
                                              session_factory = function() ChromoteSession$new())

# The browser-backed districts use a shared Chromote session because their
# Apptegy/CyberSchool pages require JavaScript to render (a plain httr2
# request receives a bot-challenge shell). Since edjobs 0.18.0 (2026-11-14)
# the Apptegy districts (registry Platform "Apptegy" / "ApptegyPageBuilder")
# go through one family routine, edjobs::fetch_apptegy_postings(), with
# optional per-district rules from the registry (List_Start/List_Stop/List_Skip); Shelby and Geyser
# ("ApptegyBespoke") keep their own scrapers (APPTEGY_DISTRICT_SCRAPERS).
# Each district is independently wrapped by fetch_apptegy_k12_postings() and
# logs as "Apptegy/chromote: <District>", so a changed page is logged without
# discarding healthy districts' results. The outer safe_scrape() protects the
# pipeline if the shared session itself cannot start.
apptegy_scrapers <- c(apptegy_family_scrapers(registry, read_k12_list_rules()), APPTEGY_DISTRICT_SCRAPERS)
apptegy_raw <- safe_scrape(
  "Apptegy/chromote K-12 districts (registry Platform Apptegy, ApptegyPageBuilder, ApptegyBespoke)",
  scrape_fn = function() fetch_apptegy_k12_postings(chromote_session_factory = function() ChromoteSession$new(),
                                                    scrapers = apptegy_scrapers),
  expected_cols = c("Title", "Location", "Posted_Date", "Link", "District")
)
if (nrow(apptegy_raw) > 0) {
  apptegy_df <- apptegy_raw %>%
    # A few Apptegy pages state pay; the rest get NA.
    ensure_posted_pay_columns() %>%
    transmute(title = Title, date_posted = Posted_Date, position = NA_character_,
              location = Location, url = Link, District,
              Posting_Source = "Apptegy district site (direct board)",
              Pay_Min, Pay_Max, Pay_Unit, Pay_Text)
} else {
  apptegy_df <- data.frame(title = character(0), date_posted = character(0), position = character(0),
                            location = character(0), url = character(0), District = character(0),
                            Posting_Source = character(0))
}
```

### OPI "Jobs for Teachers" statewide fallback feed
```{r k12 opi statewide feed, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
library(dplyr)
library(edjobs)
source("direct_api_scrapers.R")

# Montana's analog of Wyoming's WSBA vacancies page. OPI is a statewide
# supplementary source, including direct-scraper cities, but its publication
# rules and completeness have not been independently established. It stays
# intact here; exact posting-level overlaps with direct boards are removed
# only after every source's date fields have been standardized below. This
# avoids losing independent employers that happen to share a city with a
# covered district.
opi_raw <- safe_scrape(
  "OPI Jobs for Teachers (statewide)",
  scrape_fn = fetch_opi_statewide_postings,
  expected_cols = c("Title", "Location", "Posted_Date", "Link")
)

# Pay_* is the pay each posting's own detail view states and OPI_District
# the employer's district it names (both fetched by
# fetch_opi_statewide_postings()); a failed scrape's placeholder has neither.
opi_df <- ensure_posted_pay_columns(opi_raw)
if (!"OPI_District" %in% names(opi_df)) opi_df$OPI_District <- rep(NA_character_, nrow(opi_df))
for (col in c("OPI_Website", "OPI_School", "OPI_Description")) {
  if (!col %in% names(opi_df)) opi_df[[col]] <- rep(NA_character_, nrow(opi_df))
}
if (nrow(opi_df) > 0) {
  # District is NOT a canonical legal district name here -- OPI's feed only
  # exposes a City column, so District is that raw City value passed
  # through, the closest available proxy (same honesty tradeoff as every
  # other source's raw `location` field, just one level up). Since 2026-11-01 the
  # posting's own page names its district (OPI_District; METHODS.md).
  opi_df <- opi_df %>%
    transmute(title = Title, date_posted = Posted_Date, position = NA_character_,
              location = Location, url = Link, District = Location,
              Posting_Source = "OPI Jobs for Teachers (statewide)",
              Close_Date = if ("Close_Date" %in% names(.)) Close_Date else NA_character_,   # grid "Closing Date"
              Pay_Min, Pay_Max, Pay_Unit, Pay_Text, OPI_District, OPI_Website, OPI_School, OPI_Description)
} else {
  opi_df <- ensure_posted_pay_columns(
    data.frame(title = character(0), date_posted = character(0), position = character(0),
               location = character(0), url = character(0), District = character(0),
               Posting_Source = character(0), OPI_District = character(0),
               OPI_Website = character(0), OPI_School = character(0), OPI_Description = character(0)))
}
```

### LLM-extraction SHADOW pilot (quarantined -- not in the dashboard)
```{r k12 llm-extract shadow pilot, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
library(dplyr)
library(chromote)
library(edjobs)
source("history_accumulator.R")

# SHADOW PILOT -- see LLM_EXTRACT.md. Districts listed in
# llm_extract_targets.csv have their free-text-prose employment pages read
# by an LLM (Gemini, GEMINI_API_KEY; edjobs llm_extract_scraper.R) and the result written to
# Mt_Ed_Jobs/llm_extract_shadow.csv ONLY. Nothing in this chunk feeds
# combinedclean.csv, hedata.xlsx, the map, the weekly totals, or any file
# app.R reads -- so it cannot affect the live dashboard or the sanity/
# schema/drift checks. A complete no-op when the target list is empty or
# GEMINI_API_KEY is unset. The per-district outcomes are still written to
# scrape_log.csv (source "LLMExtract: <district>") for weekly review.
llm_shadow_raw <- safe_scrape(
  "LLMExtract shadow pilot (session)",
  scrape_fn = function() fetch_all_llm_extracted_postings(
    chromote_session_factory = function() ChromoteSession$new()
  ),
  expected_cols = c("Title", "Location", "Posted_Date", "Link", "District")
)

if (nrow(llm_shadow_raw) > 0) {
  # tryCatch so a problem accumulating the SHADOW file can never halt the
  # real pipeline -- this whole block is off to the side.
  tryCatch({
    llm_shadow_week <- llm_shadow_raw %>%
      transmute(
        title = Title, location = Location, date_posted = Posted_Date,
        url = Link, District,
        Posting_Source = "LLM-extracted district prose page (SHADOW -- not in dashboard)",
        Archive_Date = as.character(Sys.Date())
      )
    if (!dir.exists("Mt_Ed_Jobs")) dir.create("Mt_Ed_Jobs")
    llm_shadow <- append_weekly_rows(
      file.path("Mt_Ed_Jobs", "llm_extract_shadow.csv"), llm_shadow_week)
    write.csv(llm_shadow, file.path("Mt_Ed_Jobs", "llm_extract_shadow.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  }, error = function(e) message("LLM shadow accumulation skipped: ", conditionMessage(e)))
}
```

### Combine all K-12 data, classify, archive, and accumulate history
```{r k12 district crosswalk, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
# Every Montana public district (NCES CCD directory: name = OPI's naming,
# coordinates, staffing), tied to the registry district whose job board
# covers it, or to none (build_mt_district_crosswalk(), opi_reconcile.R).
# The combine step below uses it to decide which OPI postings count. A
# failed or implausible refresh keeps last run's file (write_reference_file()).
library(edjobs)
source("ccd_lea_pairs.R")   # MT_CCD_LEA_MAP, the crosswalk's pair input
source("opi_reconcile.R")
crosswalk_path <- file.path("Mt_Ed_Jobs", "mt_district_crosswalk.csv")
tryCatch({
  ccd_latest <- find_latest_ccd_directory_year()
  xw_new <- build_mt_district_crosswalk(ccd_latest$data,
                                        read_k12_registry(),
                                        MT_CCD_LEA_MAP)
  xw_new$CCD_Year <- rep(as.character(ccd_latest$year), nrow(xw_new))
  write_reference_file(xw_new, crosswalk_path, retrieved_source = "Urban CCD")
}, error = function(e) message("District crosswalk refresh failed: ", conditionMessage(e)))
district_crosswalk <- read.csv(crosswalk_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, colClasses = c(LEAID = "character"))
```

```{r combine k12 data, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(stringr)
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)

# standardize_date() is in edjobs (phase 5 close-out, 2026-11-16).

standardize_df_date <- function(df) {
  if (is.null(df)) return(NULL)
  if ("date_posted" %in% names(df)) {
    if (nrow(df) == 0) {
      df$date_posted <- as.Date(character(0))
    } else {
      df$date_posted <- standardize_date(df$date_posted)
    }
  }
  df
}

opi_df <- opi_df %>% mutate(date_posted = standardize_date(date_posted))

direct_dfs <- c(
  list(applitrack_df, schoolspring_df, tylerportico_df, tedk12_df, redrover_df, st_labre_df),
  direct_board_dfs,   # scrape_registry_platforms(), in MT_DIRECT_BOARD_PLATFORMS's order
  list(apptegy_df)
)
direct_dfs <- lapply(direct_dfs, standardize_df_date)
direct_df <- bind_rows(direct_dfs)
# Stale board ads (edjobs flag_stale_board_postings(); Mike, 2026-11-24): a
# board posting whose posted date, or stated closing date, is before the July 1
# that began the previous school year is flagged in Stale_Reason and not
# counted, except standing pools and ongoing roles (bus, para, custodial, food
# service, athletic coaches). The raw archive keeps it. Flagged here, before the
# OPI reconcile, so a stale ad can't stand in for a current OPI posting of the
# job; it stays among the board postings close_opi_lost_twins() checks below.
direct_df <- flag_stale_board_postings(direct_df, Sys.Date())
message(sprintf("Stale board ads: %d of %d board posting(s) flagged (not counted).",
                sum(is_stale_flagged(direct_df$Stale_Reason)), nrow(direct_df)))
# Postings a public record shows as filled (filled_postings_record.csv, edjobs filled_record(); 2026-11-26): a board
# can keep an ad up after the hire (Custer's PE and Vo-Ag jobs, hired per its July and August board agendas). The
# board row is flagged like a stale ad (not counted; the archive and the posting spells keep it), and the OPI copy is
# dropped in the reconcile below with the same reason.
filled_rec <- mt_filled_record()
filled_why <- filled_record_reason(direct_df, filled_rec, Sys.Date())
direct_df$Stale_Reason <- ifelse(is_stale_flagged(direct_df$Stale_Reason), direct_df$Stale_Reason, filled_why)
message(sprintf("Filled per public record: %d board posting(s) flagged (not counted).", sum(!is.na(filled_why))))
# OPI vs. our direct scrapes (opi_reconcile.R), posting by posting: an OPI
# posting that is the same opening as a posting on its district's board isn't
# counted (the board posting gets Also_On_OPI); every other OPI posting counts
# and is listed in the QC report. OPI's repeat listings of one job count once.
# The raw archive keeps every OPI row (OPI_Counted, OPI_Drop_Reason,
# OPI_School, OPI_Description).
opi_rec <- reconcile_opi_with_direct(opi_df, direct_df, district_crosswalk, registry, filled_record = filled_rec)
write.csv(opi_rec$qc, "mt_discrepancy_report.csv", row.names = FALSE)
adoption <- opi_rec$adoption
if (nrow(adoption) > 0) {
  sites <- opi_rec$opi_keep %>%
    filter(!is.na(OPI_Website), nzchar(OPI_Website)) %>%
    distinct(District, OPI_Website) %>%
    group_by(District) %>%
    summarize(Website = paste(OPI_Website, collapse = " ; "), .groups = "drop")
  adoption$Website <- sites$Website[match(adoption$Map_Entity, sites$District)]
}
write.csv(adoption, "opi_adoption_candidates.csv", row.names = FALSE)
direct_df <- opi_rec$direct_df %>% mutate(OPI_Counted = TRUE)
opi_df <- bind_rows(opi_rec$opi_keep %>% mutate(OPI_Counted = TRUE),
                    opi_rec$opi_dropped %>% mutate(OPI_Counted = FALSE)) %>%
  select(-any_of("OPI_Website"))

# The raw archive keeps every OPI posting (OPI_Counted = FALSE for those at a
# district we scrape) so the drift check still sees OPI's whole feed and the
# raw record stays complete; everything downstream counts OPI_Counted rows.
combined_all <- bind_rows(direct_df, opi_df) %>%
  mutate(Close_Date = if ("Close_Date" %in% names(.)) as.character(Close_Date) else NA_character_,
    across(c(title, position, location, url, District, Posting_Source), normalize_posting_text),
    Archive_Date = Sys.Date()
  )
# A posting with no place takes its district's town when all the district's schools are in one town (edjobs
# fill_k12_locations(), CCD towns in Mt_Ed_Jobs/district_towns.csv; as Wyoming since 2026-11-26). A board's or OPI's
# place is kept: OPI's town is not corrected (measured 2026-11-28: it would rewrite 35 OPI towns, some wrongly).
# Before the posting identity, which includes the place. claude-notes/2026-11-28_mt-district-towns/README.md.
district_towns <- refresh_district_towns()
combined_all <- fill_k12_locations(combined_all, district_towns, setNames(registry$NCES_LEAID, registry$District))
message(sprintf("Places from district towns: %d filled.", attr(combined_all, "location_changes")[["filled"]]))
combined_all <- combined_all %>%
  # Detail a board put in the title (a requirement, the pay, "Open Until
  # Filled", a file name) is cut off, and fills Posted Pay where the row has
  # none (edjobs); before the identity, so it's built from
  # the cleaned title.
  move_title_detail() %>%
  add_k12_posting_identity() %>%
  distinct(Posting_ID, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  attach_opi_matched_ids()
# An OPI posting whose twin on the district's own board was taken down since
# the previous run is closed (opi_reconcile.R, close_opi_lost_twins(); Mike,
# 2026-11-10: a candidate can't apply through the district any more). The
# link is each OPI posting's latest one in any earlier archive
# (opi_links_from_archives(); recomputed for archives written before
# OPI_Matched_Posting_ID existed). A failure leaves this run as matched.
combined_all <- tryCatch({
  prev_files <- sort(list.files("Archivek12_Data", pattern = "^combined_\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}\\.csv$"))
  prev_files <- prev_files[prev_files < paste0("combined_", Sys.Date(), ".csv")]
  if (length(prev_files) == 0) combined_all else {
    prev <- opi_links_from_archives(file.path("Archivek12_Data", prev_files), district_crosswalk, registry)
    out <- close_opi_lost_twins(combined_all, prev)
    n_closed <- attr(out, "opi_twins_closed"); if (is.null(n_closed)) n_closed <- 0L
    message(sprintf("OPI twins closed: %d OPI posting(s) whose board posting (matched in an earlier run, through %s) is gone are not counted.",
                    n_closed, sub("^combined_(.*)\\.csv$", "\\1", utils::tail(prev_files, 1))))
    # The QC report listed them as counted OPI postings; they aren't now.
    gone <- out[out$OPI_Drop_Reason %in% OPI_TWIN_CLOSED_REASON, , drop = FALSE]
    if (nrow(gone) > 0 && nrow(opi_rec$qc) > 0) {
      qkey <- paste(opi_rec$qc$District, opi_rec$qc$Title, opi_rec$qc$Date_Posted)
      write.csv(opi_rec$qc[!qkey %in% paste(gone$District, gone$title, gone$date_posted), , drop = FALSE],
                "mt_discrepancy_report.csv", row.names = FALSE)
    }
    out
  }
}, error = function(e) { message("OPI twin check failed, nothing closed: ", conditionMessage(e)); combined_all })
combined <- combined_all %>% filter(OPI_Counted, !is_stale_flagged(Stale_Reason))

if (!dir.exists("Archivek12_Data")) dir.create("Archivek12_Data")
file_name <- paste0("combined_", Sys.Date(), ".csv")
write.csv(combined_all, file = file.path("Archivek12_Data", file_name), row.names = FALSE)

# How SchoolSpring postings that left the board ended (filled / canceled /
# review), from each posting's own record; posting-dates plan step 4. Reads
# the raw archives just written; a failure here never stops the run.
tryCatch(refresh_schoolspring_endings("Archivek12_Data", "schoolspring_endings.csv"),
         error = function(e) message("SchoolSpring endings not updated: ", conditionMessage(e)))

# The labeled fallbacks for postings that state no pay (edjobs 0.98.0): BLS OEWS regional pay by role, fetched only
# when BLS publishes a new year, and QCEW average pay of public school employees by county (the map popup's county
# context). A failed, partial or implausible refresh keeps the committed file and is logged.
library(edjobs)
oews_wages <- refresh_pay_benchmarks()
district_county <- read_k12_registry()[, c("District", "County")]
source("opi_finance_scraper.R")
# Each OPI district's county, from OPI's finance workbook, so OPI rows naming
# their district (OPI_District) get a local OEWS area rather than the
# statewide one. A failed fetch keeps the committed file.
opi_counties_path <- file.path("Mt_Ed_Jobs", "opi_district_counties.csv")
tryCatch(write_reference_file(fetch_opi_district_counties(), opi_counties_path),
         error = function(e) log_reference_result(opi_counties_path, "error", conditionMessage(e)))
opi_counties <- read.csv(opi_counties_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Placeholder board entries ("Sample Certified Position", account-creation
# templates) are kept in the raw archive above but never counted as jobs.
# Pay_* is the pay the posting itself states (extract_posted_pay()); NA where
# the source states none or the amount is implausible for its unit
# (drop_implausible_pay(); the raw archive above keeps it as scraped). Est_* is
# the BLS regional median for the posting's role, matched to its district's
# county: the registry's, else (OPI rows) the county of the district its
# detail page names; statewide where neither is known.
# mt_k12_combinedclean() (history_accumulator.R; edjobs::build_k12_combinedclean()) is shared with
# scripts/rebuild_k12_history_from_archive.R, so a rebuild reproduces this.
source("history_accumulator.R")
combinedclean <- mt_k12_combinedclean(combined, oews_wages, district_county, opi_counties)

if (!dir.exists("Mt_Ed_Jobs")) dir.create("Mt_Ed_Jobs")
write.csv(combinedclean, file = file.path("Mt_Ed_Jobs", "combinedclean.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# The K-12 history files (teacher rows, district and job-type weekly totals, allsum, allnow), appended in one
# call (edjobs 0.96.0); scripts/rebuild_k12_history_from_archive.R builds them with the same build_k12_history().
# Counted by distinct Posting_ID.
write_k12_history(combinedclean, "Mt_Ed_Jobs", id_col = "Posting_ID")
```

### K-12 teacher salary (MT DLI Teacher Compensation Report) and staffing (CCD teacher FTE via Urban Institute)
```{r k12 salary and staffing data, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
library(dplyr)
library(edjobs)
source("salary_scrapers.R")

teacher_salary <- safe_scrape(
  "MT DLI teacher compensation", retrieved_source = "MT DLI", app_dir = "Mt_Ed_Jobs",
  scrape_fn = fetch_dli_teacher_compensation_all_districts,
  expected_cols = c("District", "Teacher_Count", "Teacher_Salary_10th_Pctile",
                     "Teacher_Avg_Salary", "Teacher_Salary_90th_Pctile", "Salary_Year")
)

# Static geo/link fields (County, Latitude, Longitude, Job_Link) come from
# the district registry -- salarymap2.csv doesn't exist as its own separate
# hand-maintained file the way Wyoming's does (this project's registry
# already carries the same hand-maintained columns). A failed fetch leaves
# last run's good salary/staffing values untouched rather than blanking
# them out, same "leave it alone, don't blank it out" behavior every other
# salary/staffing chunk in this pipeline has (see Wyoming's equivalent
# chunks) -- so salarymap2.csv is read back first (if it exists) rather
# than rebuilt fresh from the registry every run.
registry <- read_k12_registry() %>%
  select(District, any_of("NCES_LEAID"), County, Latitude, Longitude, Job_Link)

salarymap2_path <- file.path("Mt_Ed_Jobs", "salarymap2.csv")
salarymap2 <- if (file.exists(salarymap2_path)) {
  read.csv(salarymap2_path, fileEncoding = "UTF-8") %>%
    # NCES_LEAID comes from the registry too; keeping last run's copy here made
    # the join emit NCES_LEAID.x/.y (and a third copy the run after).
    select(-any_of(c("County", "Latitude", "Longitude", "Job_Link")), -starts_with("NCES_LEAID")) %>%
    right_join(registry, by = "District") %>%
    select(District, any_of("NCES_LEAID"), County, Latitude, Longitude, Job_Link, everything())
} else {
  registry
}

if (nrow(teacher_salary) > 0) {
  salarymap2 <- salarymap2 %>%
    select(-any_of(c("Teacher_Count", "Teacher_Salary_10th_Pctile", "Teacher_Avg_Salary",
                      "Teacher_Salary_90th_Pctile", "Salary_Year", "Salary_Source"))) %>%
    left_join(teacher_salary, by = "District") %>%
    # The source line only where DLI gave this district a figure: the map popup shows it under the salary, and a
    # district DLI doesn't report (suppressed or no row) would otherwise show a source with no salary (2026-11-19).
    mutate(Salary_Source = ifelse(is.na(Teacher_Avg_Salary), NA_character_,
                                  "MT Dept. of Labor & Industry Teacher Compensation Report (lmi.mt.gov/publications)"))

  # Starts building a multi-year K-12 salary trend -- MT DLI has no public
  # historical archive (only the current edition's PDFs are ever
  # published, confirmed live). Complete snapshots are idempotent while a
  # partial prior district/year set is safely backfilled.
  archive_k12_salary_snapshot(salarymap2, file.path("Mt_Ed_Jobs", "k12_salary_history.csv"),
                              MT_K12_SALARY_HISTORY_COLUMNS)
} else {
  message("MT DLI teacher compensation fetch failed -- leaving salarymap2.csv's salary columns untouched this run.")
}

# NCES_LEAID is text from read_k12_registry() (edjobs 0.113.0); write.csv() would quote it, changing every line of
# the file. Keep the committed file's quoting (the values are the same).
if (file.exists(salarymap2_path)) {
  write_csv_keep_quoting(salarymap2, salarymap2_path)
} else {
  write.csv(salarymap2, salarymap2_path, row.names = FALSE)
}

# CCD teacher FTE and enrollment, every district the crosswalk ties to CCD, hand map entries first (edjobs 0.98.0;
# a failed fetch leaves the columns alone).
refresh_ccd_teacher_fte(crosswalk_leaids(district_crosswalk))

# Which districts are read from something less than a structured platform (k12_district_coverage_tiers(),
# misc_district_scrapers.R); the rest are "Full". A fact about the registry, so it runs whether or not a fetch failed.
source("misc_district_scrapers.R")
refresh_data_coverage(k12_district_coverage_tiers())
```

### K-12 county-level context (income, rent, mining/energy employment share, population trend) and district-level child poverty rate, from the Census Bureau
```{r k12 census county and district context, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
library(dplyr)
library(edjobs)
source("opi_finance_scraper.R")

# CENSUS_API_KEY must be set (a GitHub Actions secret in CI, .Renviron
# locally). safe_scrape() catches a missing/invalid key the same way it
# catches any other fetch failure: logs it, leaves salarymap2.csv untouched
# this run, rather than crashing the whole pipeline.
# edjobs::refresh_county_context() (0.47.0): fetch through safe_scrape(), then swap the ACS columns in the file;
# a failed fetch leaves the file untouched. County names follow state_config(county_suffix = ).
county_context <- refresh_county_context("salarymap2.csv", "Census ACS county context (MT)")

# edjobs::refresh_file_columns() (0.49.0): fetch, swap the SAIPE columns by District, then Census's approximate 90%
# range from the district's size (add_saipe_range(); Mike, 2026-11-15). A failed fetch leaves the file alone.
refresh_file_columns("salarymap2.csv", "Census SAIPE district child poverty rate (MT)",
                     fetch = function() fetch_census_saipe_child_poverty(crosswalk_leaids(district_crosswalk)),   # by NCES id, pairs pooled
                     expected_cols = c("District", "Child_Poverty_Rate", "SAIPE_Year", "SAIPE_Population"), by = "District",
                     replace = c("Child_Poverty_Rate", "SAIPE_Year", "SAIPE_Population", "Child_Poverty_Low", "Child_Poverty_High"),
                     retrieved_source = "Census SAIPE", then = add_saipe_range)

refresh_file_columns("salarymap2.csv", "OPI per-district General Fund expenditures (MT)",
                     fetch = function() fetch_opi_district_expenditures(
                       lea_map = crosswalk_lea_names(district_crosswalk, MT_OPI_FINANCE_LEA_MAP),
                       county_map = crosswalk_counties(district_crosswalk)),
                     expected_cols = c("District", "Total_General_Fund_Expenditure", "Finance_FY"), by = "District",
                     replace = c("Total_General_Fund_Expenditure", "Finance_FY", "Finance_Source"),
                     retrieved_source = "OPI finance",
                     then = function(d) dplyr::mutate(d, Finance_Source = "OPI School Finance Data Files (opi.mt.gov/Leadership/Finance-Grants/School-Finance/OPI-Financial-Data-Files)"))

# Free/reduced-price lunch share beside SAIPE's child poverty rate, for every
# map entity at once: registry districts (crosswalk LEAIDs; a district the
# crosswalk doesn't tie yet uses its registry NCES id) and the OPI-only
# districts below (edjobs::fetch_ccd_frl_share(); each entity's
# newest reporting year). salarymap2.csv keeps last run's values on a failure.
frl_registry <- read_k12_registry()
frl_ids <- crosswalk_leaids(district_crosswalk)
untied <- setdiff(frl_registry$District, names(frl_ids))
frl_ids[untied] <- as.list(as.character(frl_registry$NCES_LEAID[match(untied, frl_registry$District)]))
opi_only_xw <- district_crosswalk[is.na(district_crosswalk$Registry_District), , drop = FALSE]
frl_ids <- c(frl_ids, lapply(split(as.character(opi_only_xw$LEAID), opi_only_xw$Map_Entity), unique))
frl_ids <- frl_ids[!vapply(frl_ids, function(x) all(is.na(x)), logical(1))]
# The fetched table stays in frl_all: the OPI-only districts chunk below joins it too.
frl_all <- refresh_file_columns("salarymap2.csv", "CCD free/reduced-price lunch share (MT)",
                     fetch = function() fetch_ccd_frl_share(30, frl_ids),
                     expected_cols = c("District", "Free_Reduced_Lunch_Share", "FRL_Schools_Reporting", "FRL_Year"),
                     by = "District", retrieved_source = "Urban CCD", relationship = "many-to-one")
```

### K-12 districts we don't scrape that post on OPI (map entities with context)
```{r k12 opi-only districts, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
# The districts this week's OPI postings filled in for (case 3 in
# opi_reconcile.R) get a map dot with the same context as registry
# districts where a statewide source covers them: CCD location/staffing
# (crosswalk), DLI teacher pay (school system matched by name), SAIPE child
# poverty (NCES id), OPI finance (OPI's naming), county ACS context (copied
# from salarymap2.csv's registry districts in that county). A source whose
# fetch fails keeps last run's values for that entity.
source("opi_reconcile.R")
opi_only_path <- file.path("Mt_Ed_Jobs", "opi_only_districts.csv")
opi_only_entities <- unique(combinedclean$District[
  combinedclean$District %in% district_crosswalk$Map_Entity[is.na(district_crosswalk$Registry_District)]])

dli_systems <- safe_scrape("MT DLI teacher compensation (all school systems)", retrieved_source = "MT DLI", app_dir = "Mt_Ed_Jobs", scrape_fn = fetch_dli_all_systems,
                           expected_cols = c("DLI_Name", "Teacher_Avg_Salary"))
saipe_leaid <- safe_scrape("Census SAIPE child poverty by NCES id (MT)", retrieved_source = "Census SAIPE", app_dir = "Mt_Ed_Jobs", scrape_fn = fetch_saipe_by_leaid,
                           expected_cols = c("LEAID", "Child_Poverty_Rate"))
finance_by_name <- safe_scrape("OPI General Fund by district name (MT)", retrieved_source = "OPI finance", app_dir = "Mt_Ed_Jobs",
                               scrape_fn = function() opi_finance_by_district(fetch_opi_finance_workbook(OPI_FINANCE_CURRENT_YEAR_URL)),
                               expected_cols = c("OPI_District", "Total_General_Fund_Expenditure"))
acs_cols <- c("County", "Median_Household_Income", "Median_Gross_Rent", "Population", "ACS_Year",
              "Mining_Employment_Share", "Population_Change_Pct",
              "Median_Household_Income_MOE", "Median_Gross_Rent_MOE", "Mining_Employment_Share_MOE")
county_ctx <- read.csv(salarymap2_path, fileEncoding = "UTF-8") %>% select(any_of(acs_cols))

opi_only <- build_opi_only_districts(district_crosswalk, opi_only_entities,
                                     dli_systems = if (nrow(dli_systems) > 0) dli_systems,
                                     saipe = if (nrow(saipe_leaid) > 0) saipe_leaid,
                                     finance = if (nrow(finance_by_name) > 0) finance_by_name,
                                     county_context = county_ctx)
if (nrow(opi_only) > 0) {
  opi_only$CCD_Year <- district_crosswalk$CCD_Year[1]
  if (nrow(dli_systems) > 0) {
    opi_only$Salary_Year <- dli_systems$Salary_Year[1]
    opi_only$Salary_Source <- ifelse(is.na(opi_only$Teacher_Avg_Salary), NA_character_,
      "MT Dept. of Labor & Industry Teacher Compensation Report (lmi.mt.gov/publications)")
  }
  if (nrow(finance_by_name) > 0) {
    opi_only$Finance_Source <- "OPI School Finance Data Files (opi.mt.gov/Leadership/Finance-Grants/School-Finance/OPI-Financial-Data-Files)"
  }
  if (exists("frl_all") && nrow(frl_all) > 0) {
    opi_only <- opi_only %>%
      select(-any_of(c("Free_Reduced_Lunch_Share", "FRL_Schools_Reporting", "FRL_Year"))) %>%
      left_join(frl_all, by = "District", relationship = "many-to-one")
  }
  # A failed source this run: carry last run's values for the same entity.
  if (file.exists(opi_only_path)) {
    prev <- read.csv(opi_only_path, fileEncoding = "UTF-8", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    carry <- list(dli = c("Teacher_Count", "Teacher_Salary_10th_Pctile", "Teacher_Avg_Salary",
                          "Teacher_Salary_90th_Pctile", "DLI_Name", "Salary_Year", "Salary_Source"),
                  saipe = c("Child_Poverty_Rate", "SAIPE_Year", "SAIPE_Population"),
                  fin = c("Total_General_Fund_Expenditure", "Finance_FY", "Finance_Source"),
                  frl = c("Free_Reduced_Lunch_Share", "FRL_Schools_Reporting", "FRL_Year"))
    failed <- c(dli = nrow(dli_systems) == 0, saipe = nrow(saipe_leaid) == 0, fin = nrow(finance_by_name) == 0,
                frl = !exists("frl_all") || nrow(frl_all) == 0)
    for (src in names(failed)[failed]) for (col in intersect(carry[[src]], names(prev))) {
      opi_only[[col]] <- prev[[col]][match(opi_only$District, prev$District)]
    }
  }
}
# Employers that aren't public districts (co-ops, a hospital school, the
# Northern Cheyenne Tribal School, private schools): one map row each from
# other_employers.csv (build_other_employer_rows(), opi_reconcile.R).
other_spec <- read.csv("other_employers.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE, colClasses = c(Source_ID = "character"))
others <- build_other_employer_rows(other_spec, unique(combinedclean$District),
                                    saipe = if (nrow(saipe_leaid) > 0) saipe_leaid,
                                    county_context = county_ctx,
                                    district_names = setNames(district_crosswalk$Map_Entity, district_crosswalk$LEAID),
                                    previous = if (file.exists(opi_only_path)) read.csv(opi_only_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
# The surrounding-district lookups go in scrape_log.csv: an error when the
# Census geocoder failed for any employer (last run's rate kept for those).
geo_failed <- attr(others, "geocode_failed")
log_scrape_result("Census geocoder (surrounding-district poverty, other employers)",
                  status = if (length(geo_failed)) "error" else "ok",
                  n_rows = sum(!is.na(others$Child_Poverty_Basis)),
                  error_message = if (length(geo_failed)) paste("geocoder failed for:", paste(geo_failed, collapse = "; ")) else NA_character_)
if (!length(geo_failed)) record_source_retrieved("Census Geocoder", "Mt_Ed_Jobs")
# CCD_Year is text: a private school's record year is "2023-24" (PSS).
opi_only <- dplyr::bind_rows(dplyr::mutate(complete_opi_only_columns(opi_only), CCD_Year = as.character(CCD_Year)),
                             dplyr::mutate(others, CCD_Year = as.character(CCD_Year)))
# Any other employer with postings and no map row goes to the weekly drift issue.
unmapped <- unmapped_employers(combinedclean$District, registry$District, opi_only_entities, other_spec)
write.csv(data.frame(District = unmapped,
                     Postings = as.integer(table(combinedclean$District)[unmapped]), stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
          "unmapped_employers.csv", row.names = FALSE)
# Census's approximate 90% range beside each child poverty estimate (edjobs::add_saipe_range()).
write.csv(complete_opi_only_columns(add_saipe_range(opi_only)), opi_only_path, row.names = FALSE)
```


## Part 2: Montana Higher Ed Data

### HE institutions scraped directly (PeopleAdmin, JazzHR, Paycom, heuristic sources)
```{r he direct-platform institutions, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
library(dplyr)
library(chromote)
library(edjobs)
source("direct_api_scrapers.R")
source("misc_college_scrapers.R")

he_registry <- read_he_registry()

# Every college board with a registry platform, read by edjobs::scrape_registry_platforms() (edjobs 0.94.0; review
# step 5 slice B, 2026-11-24) as the K-12 chunk reads its boards: each registry row is scraped with its scraper_spec()
# from state_config.R, one group per platform in MT_HE_PLATFORMS's order. `shape = "raw"` keeps each scraper's own
# columns (dates are parsed in the munge chunk) and adds Institution, except where the scraper set it: JazzHR's
# parser attributes each posting to its real institution (Montana Tech or Highlands College, 2026-08-07). NEOGOV's
# board "ummissoula" also carries Helena College, Missoula College and UM Western (SharesBoard registry rows), so
# its postings are given their own institution by Location_Pattern (assign_shared_board_institutions()).
he_board_dfs <- scrape_registry_platforms(
  he_registry, MT_HE_PLATFORMS, source = "he_institution_registry.csv", shape = "raw",
  session_factory = function() ChromoteSession$new(),
  expected_cols = list(JazzHR = c("Title", "Location", "Posted_Date", "Link", "Institution")),
  after = list(Neogov = function(df, row) assign_shared_board_institutions(df, row$Feed_URL, he_registry))
)

# University of Montana's faculty jobs are on Interfolio (tenant 53871), not
# NEOGOV: every UM and Missoula College faculty search (UM HR's faculty
# hiring page, 2026-11-21; direct_api_scrapers.R). A second source for UM's
# registry row, logged under its own name; the coverage calendar below lists
# it in extra_sources, so UM counts as healthy only when both scrapes are. A
# posting whose unit is one of the UM-board campuses (registry SharesBoard
# rows on "ummissoula": Missoula College, Helena College, UM Western) goes to
# that institution by the same Location_Pattern, read against its unit.
UM_INTERFOLIO_TENANT <- "53871"
UM_INTERFOLIO_SOURCE <- "University of Montana (Interfolio faculty)"
interfolio_df <- safe_scrape(
  UM_INTERFOLIO_SOURCE,
  scrape_fn = function() fetch_interfolio_postings(UM_INTERFOLIO_TENANT),
  expected_cols = c("Title", "Location", "Posted_Date", "Link")
)
if (nrow(interfolio_df) > 0) {
  interfolio_df$Institution <- "University of Montana"
  interfolio_df <- assign_shared_board_institutions(interfolio_df, "ummissoula", he_registry, location_col = "Unit")
  interfolio_df$Unit <- NULL
}

standardize_he_df_date <- function(df) {
  if (is.null(df)) return(NULL)
  if ("Posted_Date" %in% names(df)) {
    df$Posted_Date <- as.character(df$Posted_Date)
  }
  df
}

# In the old blocks' order, with Interfolio (UM faculty, read above) after NEOGOV.
he_dfs <- c(he_board_dfs[c("peopleadmin", "jazzhr", "paycom", "milescc", "dawsoncc", "isolvedhire", "neogov")],
            list(interfolio = interfolio_df),
            he_board_dfs[c("cssboard", "adp", "stonechild", "ancollege", "cdkc")])
he_dfs <- lapply(he_dfs, standardize_he_df_date)
hedata_raw <- bind_rows(he_dfs)
```

### Combine all HE data, classify, archive, and accumulate history
```{r munge he data, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
library(dplyr)
library(writexl)

# Pay_* is the pay the posting states (PeopleAdmin, isolved Hire, Paycom and
# UM's NEOGOV board carry it; every other HE source is NA). It's kept in
# hedata.xlsx and the raw archive, but not in the accumulated facultydata.csv
# below.
# Close_Date: PeopleAdmin's own close date (or "Open Until Filled") and NEOGOV's stated closing
# date (each posting's page; edjobs 0.11.0); NA for other HE sources.
hedata <- combine_he_frames(hedata_raw)

# Where each posting goes on the map (edjobs place_he_postings(), 2026-11-16):
# a posting is placed at another MT town only when the posting itself names
# that town: its Location (FVCC's "Libby, MT"), a title marker ("*Havre, MT*"),
# its department when that is a fixed site (he_campus_departments.csv: MSU's
# research centers, each with its source), or an explicit sentence on its
# PeopleAdmin page (Page_Places: "This position is located in Joliet, Montana";
# edjobs 0.34.0). Towns come from places.csv (every Census place in the state,
# its point and county). Anything else (the main campus town, a department,
# "United States", several towns, another state) stays at the main campus;
# Place_Basis says which, for the map's note. Page_Places is dropped there.
hedata <- place_he_postings(hedata, he_registry, read_state_places("places.csv"), "MT",
                            campus_departments = read.csv("he_campus_departments.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE))

if (!dir.exists("Archived_HE_Data")) dir.create("Archived_HE_Data")
if (!dir.exists("Mt_Ed_Jobs")) dir.create("Mt_Ed_Jobs")

file_name <- paste0("hedata_", Sys.Date(), ".xlsx")
write_xlsx(hedata, path = file.path("Archived_HE_Data", file_name))

# Posting status (posting_status.R; closing-date audit 2026-11-05): every
# posting with a checkable page (AppliTrack, TalentEd, Red Rover, NEOGOV,
# JazzHR, Paycom) that dropped off its board since the last run, K-12 and
# higher ed, recorded in posting_status.csv: whether the platform says it
# closed, and the closing date it states. A failure here never stops the run.
library(edjobs)
tryCatch(refresh_posting_status("Archivek12_Data", "Archived_HE_Data", "posting_status.csv",
                                session_factory = function() chromote::ChromoteSession$new()),
         error = function(e) message("Posting status not updated: ", conditionMessage(e)))

# Coverage calendar (posting-dates plan step 2): every source's outcome this
# run (ok / empty / error / not_logged), so a posting that stops appearing is
# read as ended only when its source was healthy. Every source has been
# scraped by now; a failure here never stops the run.
library(edjobs)
tryCatch(refresh_coverage_calendar(
  "coverage_calendar.csv", "scrape_log.csv",
  k12_entities = read_k12_registry()$District,
  he_entities = read_he_registry()$Institution,
  data_k12 = unique(combined_all$District), data_he = unique(hedata$Institution),
  feeds = c("OPI statewide feed" = "^OPI Jobs for Teachers",
            "Apptegy browser session (all Apptegy districts)" = "^Apptegy/chromote K-12 districts"),
  # No board of their own: their postings come from the parent's board.
  shared_boards = c("Highlands College" = "Montana Tech", "Helena College" = "University of Montana",
                    "Missoula College" = "University of Montana",
                    "University of Montana Western" = "University of Montana"),
  # UM's faculty jobs come from a second scrape (Interfolio, above): UM and the
  # boards it shares are healthy only when both ran fine (edjobs 0.72.0).
  extra_sources = list("University of Montana" = UM_INTERFOLIO_SOURCE)),
  error = function(e) message("Coverage calendar not updated: ", conditionMessage(e)))
# Non-postings ("Job Title" headers, "No Jobs" notices) stay in the raw archive above but are dropped from
# everything shown or counted, implausible posted pay is blanked, and staff postings that state no pay get the
# institution's IPEDS average for their staff category (ipeds_staff_salaries.csv from the previous run), added
# after the raw archive write (edjobs finish_he_rows()).
hedata <- finish_he_rows(hedata, "Mt_Ed_Jobs", canonicalize_he_institution)
write_xlsx(hedata, path = file.path("Mt_Ed_Jobs", "hedata.xlsx"))

# Fix historical institution-name typos before anything downstream keys off
# Institution -- applied AFTER the xlsx archive writes above, so the
# archived raw snapshot keeps whatever spelling the scraper actually
# produced that week.
hedata <- hedata %>% mutate(Institution = canonicalize_he_institution(Institution))

# The higher-ed history files (faculty rows, institution and job-type weekly totals, allsum_he, allnow_he), appended
# in one call (edjobs 0.97.0); scripts/rebuild_he_history_from_archive.R builds them with the same build_he_history().
write_he_history(hedata, "Mt_Ed_Jobs")
```

### HE faculty salary, enrollment, and Pell Grant recipient share (IPEDS via Urban Institute)
```{r he salary enrollment pell data, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
library(dplyr)
library(edjobs)
source("ipeds_unitids.R")   # IPEDS_UNITID_MAP; the fetchers are in edjobs

# IPEDS staff pay by category (edjobs 0.98.0): the labeled fallback for college staff postings that state no pay. The
# HE munge step reads it on the next run; a failed fetch keeps the existing file.
refresh_ipeds_staff_pay()

# Static geo/link fields (Name/County/Latitude/Longitude/Link) come from
# he_institution_registry.csv, the same "read salarymap.csv back first if
# it exists, don't blank out a failed fetch's columns" pattern
# salarymap2.csv's chunk above uses.
he_registry <- read_he_registry() %>%
  transmute(Name = Institution, County, Longitude, Latitude, Link = Job_Link)

salarymap_path <- file.path("Mt_Ed_Jobs", "salarymap.csv")
salarymap <- if (file.exists(salarymap_path)) {
  read.csv(salarymap_path, fileEncoding = "UTF-8") %>%
    select(-any_of(c("County", "Longitude", "Latitude", "Link"))) %>%
    right_join(he_registry, by = "Name") %>%
    select(Name, County, Longitude, Latitude, Link, everything())
} else {
  he_registry
}

write.csv(salarymap, salarymap_path, row.names = FALSE)

# Faculty salaries and the two prior years' averages from IPEDS (edjobs 0.98.0). The source line only where IPEDS gave
# a figure (Highlands College and Missoula College report under their parents); a failed fetch leaves the columns alone.
refresh_ipeds_he_salaries(IPEDS_UNITID_MAP)

# edjobs::refresh_file_columns() (0.48.0): fetch through safe_scrape(); on rows, swap these columns in salarymap.csv
# by Name; a failed fetch leaves the file (and last week's values) alone.
refresh_file_columns("salarymap.csv", "IPEDS fall enrollment FTE (MT)",
                     fetch = function() fetch_ipeds_he_enrollment(IPEDS_UNITID_MAP),
                     expected_cols = c("Name", "Enrollment", "Enrollment_Year"), by = "Name", retrieved_source = "Urban IPEDS")
refresh_file_columns("salarymap.csv", "IPEDS fall enrollment 5-year trend (MT)",
                     fetch = function() fetch_ipeds_he_enrollment_trend(IPEDS_UNITID_MAP),
                     expected_cols = c("Name", "Enrollment_Change_Pct"), by = "Name", retrieved_source = "Urban IPEDS")
refresh_file_columns("salarymap.csv", "FSA Pell Grant recipient share (MT)",
                     fetch = function() fetch_ipeds_he_pell_share(IPEDS_UNITID_MAP),
                     expected_cols = c("Name", "Pell_Recipient_Share", "Pell_Year"), by = "Name", retrieved_source = "Urban FSA")
```

```{r he census county context, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
library(dplyr)
library(edjobs)

# Reuses the exact same fetch_census_county_context() pipeline as the K-12
# chunk earlier in this file -- fetched independently rather than reusing
# that chunk's `county_context` variable, matching every other chunk in
# this file being self-contained and re-runnable on its own.
# edjobs::refresh_county_context() (0.47.0): fetch through safe_scrape(), then swap the ACS columns in the file;

county_context_he <- refresh_county_context("salarymap.csv", "Census ACS county context for HE institutions (MT)")
```
